People choose to have an abortion for many diverse and often overlapping reasons, though the vast majority result from unintended pregnancies. Common personal and socioeconomic factors include financial instability (such as being unable to afford a child), timing (feeling unready for a child at that stage of life), and wanting to focus on existing children or future career and educational goals. Relationship issues, such as an unsupportive partner or an unstable home life, also play a significant role. Additionally, some abortions are performed for medical reasons, known as Termination for Medical Reasons (TFMR), which may occur if the pregnancy poses a threat to the pregnant person’s life or health—such as from severe preeclampsia or cancer—or if there are serious fetal anomalies that mean the baby would not survive or would suffer from a severe disability.
